description.value: A structural MRI study comparing cortical thickness between male adolescents with serious substance use and conduct problems and control adolescents using ROI multiple regression and whole-cerebrum QDEC analyses.

spans.text: Accordingly, we used brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to study male youths with serious substance use and conduct problems, and controls, to search for inter-group differences in cortical thickness.

value: We hypothesized that youths with serious substance use and conduct problems would demonstrate thinner cortices in regions important for response inhibition and reward-related processing, namely in inferior frontal gyrus, OFC, and insula.
